claim: PF gives a small-to-moderate average benefit over direct instruction for conceptual understanding and transfer (g=0.36, 53 studies, 166 comparisons; high-fidelity PF 0.37-0.58). Only the originator group has pooled it, and the adjusted 0.87 is model-dependent. Abstract also says grades 2-5 and domain-general skills favoured instruction-first; quasi-experiments add to the effect; study table and lab share unread (d10).
agent_test: Not testable directly; use as prior for effect size ~0.3 at best.

claim: Effects are heterogeneous: study-level d runs from about -0.54 to 1.12, so the sign depends on design fidelity and domain.
agent_test: Run PF-first vs instruction-first on several task types; report per-type sign.

claim: Original Kapur studies (variance, kinematics, Singapore/India secondary schools) found PF beat direct instruction on conceptual and transfer items without losing procedural fluency. All were quasi-experimental, intact classes, mostly one lab.
agent_test: Attempt-first then lessons vs lessons-first on held-out hard items at equal tokens.

claim: Independent replications outside the originator lab are mixed to null: Nachtigall Study 1 favoured direct instruction (partial eta2=.12), Study 2 null (BF10=0.23); Loibl and Leuders null on Bayesian reasoning; Mazziotti null (timing F=1.01); Glogger-Frey favoured worked solution first (d=-0.72); Loibl and Leukel null in primary school. Braas 2025 (N=152) also found PF vs DI d=0.29, ns.
agent_test: Treat attempt-first as conditional; test it, do not assume it.

claim: PF fails in some replications for different reasons. Loibl and Leuders: 31 of 38 made one attempt. Nachtigall Study 1: groups made 3.93 solution ideas, yet DI won (partial eta2=.12 to .13), so attempt count alone does not explain it. Braas: 3.63 solutions, low diversity, no PF effect. Component coverage tracked outcome there (r=.418).
agent_test: Log attempts per item, distinct methods and coverage of the correct components; do not gate the lessons step on count alone.

claim: The number of distinct solution methods a learner generates predicts post-test learning more strongly than prior achievement (F=62.6 and 105.5 vs prior ns). Kapur, Saba and Roll (2023) is an association in quasi-experiments (RSMs F=62.6 and 105.5). Braas 2025 manipulated diversity of supplied attempts: VF-high beat VF-low and DI (d=0.64, 0.65) and equalled PF. So diversity is plausibly causal when supplied; own-generation count remains correlational.
agent_test: Count distinct candidate approaches before verification; correlate with accuracy on our agent.

claim: Learners in PF feel more confident than they should or report low confidence depending on study; perceived competence after the attempt phase was higher for PF than DI (3.53 vs 3.09) then fell below it (3.02 vs 3.92). Calibration drops after the consolidation phase.
agent_test: Log self-rated confidence before and after the lessons step; check calibration gap.

claim: Observing someone else's failure (vicarious failure) can match or beat doing PF: VF-high vs DI d=0.65, VF-high vs PF d=0.29 ns; Kapur 2014 found PF gave more effort and interest in canonical solution. Braas 2025 (randomised, N=152): a supplied failed attempt equalled own PF only when it covered all canonical components. LeMa: GPT-4 corrected others' errors at 26.9% to 37.5% vs its own 8.0%.
agent_test: Compare agent's own failed attempt vs a supplied failed attempt as the memory item.

claim: Consolidation that compares and contrasts student solutions with the canonical one is the necessary second half; attempt alone is not the claim.
agent_test: Ablate the compare-and-contrast step: attempt only vs attempt plus explicit lessons.

claim: Fully unguided invention is not better than guided: scaffolded vs unscaffolded problem-solving-first g=-0.08 [-0.20,0.04]; guided invention gave more conceptual features in Roll; Akgun found a pretest-then-LLM design improved final test (d=1.54, one session, preprint).
agent_test: Test scaffold level during the attempt phase at equal tokens.

claim: PF benefit is strongest for lower-prior-knowledge students in a large course (Low tercile b=8.28 percentage points, p<.001) but the final exam showed no effect (p=.668); in Chowrira the PF section had higher baseline.
agent_test: Check whether weaker base models gain more from attempt-first.

claim: Tutor LLMs steered by a PF script elicit far more student solution methods than a plain tutor (2.34 vs 1.0 simulated; 2.6 vs lower field, p=.05, N=17) and higher PF fidelity score, but learning outcome was not measured.
agent_test: Not an agent-reasoning result; do not cite as learning evidence.

claim: Prompted LLM tutors that just give answers raise practice scores but harm unaided exams (GPT Base -17%, Tutor ~0), consistent with removing productive struggle. Guardrail prompts mitigated it.
agent_test: Not a direct test; summary-level for two of three records (403 on full text).

claim: Timing of AI access matters: access only when learners had tried first (RL policy) beat always-on access (d=0.59, N=105) but did not beat no access (d=-0.07).
agent_test: Learner-side study; analogue is not clear for agent self-use.

claim: For LLM agents, learning from own failed attempts via stored verbal reflections works when a reliable success signal exists: Reflexion 130/134 ALFWorld (+22%), HotPotQA +20%, HumanEval +11%; reflection over bare trajectory memory +8% on HotPotQA; no gain on WebShop.
agent_test: Lessons-after-failure memory with an oracle check vs without.

claim: Extracting cross-task insights from successes and failures beats raw retrying: ExpeL ALFWorld 59.0 vs ReAct 40.0, HotpotQA 39.0 vs 28.0; combines with Reflexion (64.2 at round 3).
agent_test: Distilled lessons vs raw trajectory retrieval at equal prompt tokens.

claim: Without an external success signal, LLM self-correction does not help and can hurt (GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0; CommonSenseQA 84.0 to 81.5); with oracle labels it helps (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3). The lessons step needs a verifier. Reflexion: reliable tests +11 points (HumanEval 0.80 to 0.91), noisy tests (16% false pass) -3 points (MBPP 0.80 to 0.77), no tests -8 points on Rust-50 (0.60 to 0.52). Kamoi 2024 survey agrees.
agent_test: Run attempt-first-lessons memory with and without a ground-truth check.

claim: Learning from negative examples by fine-tuning helps in some settings and hurts in others depending on labeling and quality.
agent_test: Not a prompt-scaffold result; low priority.

claim: Duration and recall: PF students in a small programming study succeeded on a delayed task more often (7/7 vs 6/9) though initial attempts mostly failed (2/7 vs 8/9). Tiny N, no tests.
agent_test: Do not use for decisions.

claim: Large-course field data show a consistent participation-linked exam gain (d=0.28 to 0.59 over four years), but no control group and voluntary participation.
agent_test: Weak; self-selection.

claim: The original double-transfer result: invention-first beat tell-and-practice on a transfer problem only when the test supplied a worked-example resource (Exp 1: 60.8% vs 29.2% with resource, 30.4% vs 32.0% without; Exp 2: 45.8% vs 21.9% with, 18.2% vs 26.6% without). The gain was smaller with other teachers.
agent_test: Compare attempt-first with and without a worked solution available at test time.

claim: The closest LLM test (LEAP) of learning principles from own sampled errors with ground truth gives small, uneven accuracy gains over few-shot CoT (DROP GPT-4 +6.5 to +7.5; HotpotQA GPT-4 +3.3; GSM8K and MATH within about 1 point; some cells negative; Llama-2-70B worse). It is not an attempt-first vs instruction-first comparison and not token matched.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of own-error lessons vs correct-example-only lessons, per model.

claim: No 2020-2026 study was found that tests attempt-first vs instruction-first on LLM task accuracy at equal tokens. The closest are LEAP, Reflexion, ExpeL and multi-attempt RL (45.6% to 52.5% with a second attempt, trained with an oracle). This is absence in a limited search, not proof.
agent_test: This is the experiment to run: attempt-then-lesson vs lesson-then-attempt, same token budget.

claim: Replication failures share no single design feature: Loibl and Leuders had one attempt per student; Nachtigall had about 4 ideas per group but a non-STEM domain, no pretest and a wrong-direction Study 1; Braas had 3.63 solutions with low component coverage.
agent_test: Log attempts per item, distinct methods and component coverage in agent traces, then check which predicts the lessons-step gain.

claim: Retention beyond one week is untested against a control in the sources opened. Schwartz and Martin's one-year test (n=30, 57% still computed the mean deviation) had no control.
agent_test: Not a prompt-scaffold test; skip.

claim: No LLM study was found that measured confidence or calibration after a failed-then-instructed cycle. The human hint is Nachtigall: PF perceived competence 3.53 then 3.02, and a bigger drop went with lower learning (r=-0.36).
agent_test: Log stated confidence before and after the lessons step and score it against accuracy.
